intent: Avoid same-process concurrent save temp collision and preserve old destination before commit without new architecture.
assumptions: Callers accept last successful commit wins

architecture.A1 System context: Existing HOST document/settings save callers invoke FileSystemPort. Only real StdFileSystem implementation changes; no UI or generic save redesign.
architecture.A2 Hexagonal system boundary: Driving UI/CLI -> existing HOST use cases -> FileSystemPort <- StdFileSystem -> OS filesystem. Domain has no filesystem dependency.
architecture.A3 Module dependency: HOST -> sgenaxis-ports; sgenaxis-adapters -> sgenaxis-ports and std. No application -> concrete adapter dependency added.
architecture.A4 Responsibilities: Caller owns save intent and payload. FileSystemPort owns opaque IO contract. StdFileSystem owns one write transaction and temporary file lifecycle. OS implements rename.
architecture.A5 Input ports: Existing FileSystemPort::write_atomic(path:&str, contents:&[u8])->Result<(),PortError>; no signature changes.
architecture.A6 Output ports: No new output ports; adapter calls std::fs/OpenOptions/Write behind existing IO boundary.
architecture.A7 Driving adapters: Existing UI/CLI/HOST callers unchanged; tests call FileSystemPort.
architecture.A8 Driven adapters: StdFileSystem only. FakeFileSystem unchanged; real adapter tests establish OS-specific guarantees.
architecture.A9 Dependency direction: Caller -> existing port <- real adapter -> standard library/OS. Domain and HOST never acquire concrete filesystem dependency.
architecture.A10 State ownership: Destination is committed persistent state; caller owns submitted byte slice. Each invocation exclusively owns its temp path and open handle; no authoritative global state. Atomic counter, if used, is naming assistance only; create_new decides ownership.
architecture.A11 Mutation boundary: Only owning invocation writes/removes its temporary file. Destination changes only at successful rename. Never delete destination as replacement fallback.
architecture.A12 Transaction boundary: Create sibling exclusively -> write all -> sync file -> close -> rename over destination. Before successful rename, prior destination bytes remain unchanged. Error cleanup removes only owned temp, best effort; cannot promise cleanup if OS denies removal.
architecture.A13 External system boundary: Local filesystem behavior; Windows machine probe only. Network filesystems, adversarial directory mutation, symlink sandboxing, power loss and parent-directory fsync excluded.
architecture.A14 Forbidden dependencies: No new Manager/service/port/crate, per-target lock table, serialization change, CAS/version arbitration, background cleanup daemon, caller rewrite, public error variant, or remove-destination fallback.

contracts: Success means destination contains exactly one complete submitted payload at this invocation commit; later successful writers may replace it.
Concurrent successful writes use last successful commit wins, not request-start order. No merged/torn payload.
Before commit failure leaves previous destination unchanged; existing parent-directory creation remains allowed and is not rolled back.
Exclusive create collision never truncates existing temp. Retry bounded at 128 candidates; exhaustion returns existing PortError mapping and preserves destination.
Owned temp is closed then cleanup attempted on write/sync/rename failure. Cleanup never targets peer files or replaces primary error. Residual temp may remain if cleanup is denied.

No CAS, locking, multi-file transaction, power-loss durability or universal filesystem atomicity guarantee. Supported Windows local filesystem overwrite is tested; additional platforms require own evidence.

Deterministic barrier after both exclusively-created temp handles: both writers must reach barrier; assert different owned paths; release A commit then B commit and final bytes B; reverse ordering final A. Timeout is harness failure, not valid RED.
Place candidate collision sentinel; force first private candidate then next unused candidate; sentinel bytes unchanged and successful retry. Force 128 collisions -> error, target/sentinels unchanged.

Inject write failure after partial owned temp bytes, and sync failure independently; close, cleanup attempted, previous target exact. Inject cleanup denial -> original error retained, residue reported by harness only.
Inject rename denial; existing destination remains; owned temp removed when permitted. Never remove destination.
Peer prepares temp at barrier; failing invocation cleans up; peer temp survives and peer commits intact.
Real Windows replacement integration: existing file -> new complete bytes; target directory failure preserves directory; no owned leftovers.
Distinct target paths, nested missing parents, unicode/spaces path, bytes containing zero/invalid UTF8 preserve exact bytes; regression existing swap/host save/settings tests.
